author: bd-spin/bd-spin-20260513T044329Z-2514582
text:
Escalating after probing: OpenSSL 3.0.13 'verify' has NO 'codesign' purpose. 'openssl verify -help' lists exactly these purposes:

  sslclient, sslserver, nssslserver, smimesign, smimeencrypt, crlsign, any, ocsphelper, timestampsign

The bead description named '-purpose codesign' but that purpose doesn't exist in OpenSSL's 'verify' tool. (id-kp-codeSigning IS recognized as an EKU OID by OpenSSL elsewhere — e.g. 'openssl x509 -ext extendedKeyUsage' will print 'Code Signing' for 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.3 — but 'openssl verify -purpose' has no codesign verb.)

Three options for a human decision:

(A) RESCOPE the bead to 'OpenSSL CANNOT oracle verify_code_signer; document the gap in baseline-verify-openssl.md and close.' Cheap. The pyca diff (PKIX-fmtv.19) also has no oracle for code-signing; codesigning differential falls to ... pkilint? signtool? None of the AGENTS.md-acceptable oracles cover it.

(B) Add a chain-only diff: invoke 'openssl verify -purpose any' (or no -purpose) against the codesigning fixtures. That tests path validation but not EKU enforcement; documents OpenSSL as a 'chain-only' oracle for verify_code_signer rather than purpose-aware. Has some signal: differential testing of path validity, validity period, anchor binding.

(C) Use a custom -verify_name policy. OpenSSL's 'Recognized certificate policy names' include 'default' and 'pkcs7'; neither maps to code-signing semantics. (Note: not to be confused with -purpose.)

Recommend (A) for now: the OpenSSL CLI literally cannot oracle this wrapper's purpose-specific check. If the workspace later wants codesigning differential coverage, the right move is to add pyca's TBD code-signing verifier (if/when pyca adds one) or commission a separate test against signtool / osslsigncode. None of those are currently in the workspace's oracle vocabulary.

Releasing the claim. Bead remains open with 'human' label.
